text:
alexa: Heads-up: design review for the Roles/Invite surface tomorrow. Primary goal: reduce confusion when SSO toggle is enforced and invite language. Thinking about merging the SSO status pill into the invite drawer header and showing a contextual help link that surfaces org-wide SSO settings.
ben: Merging the pill seems cleaner, but don't hide the toggle completely. Admins need quick access to override enforcement for legacy invites (rare but real). Maybe pill + small kebab menu with "Manage SSO" and "Invite anyway (audit)".
priya: UX nit: wording for toggle. We currently say "Enforce SSO" which reads like an action. Suggest "SSO required for sign-in" for state clarity and a linked "why?".
liam: Agree on copy. Also for the invite drawer CTA, we should make the primary button clear: when SSO required, primary = "Invite via SSO"; when not required primary = "Send invite". Otherwise admins get tripped up.
alexa: Good point. Also propose inline validation when entering email: we show a subtle hint if the domain matches the org SSO domains and a tooltip "This account will be routed via your org SSO".
ben: Accessibility: ensure the SSO pill has aria-pressed or role=switch depending on control type. access-bot: Accessibility warning: if pill opens a menu, ensure keyboard focus lands in the menu and ESC closes. Provide aria-label describing enforcement implications.
priya: Invite flow edge-case: what about invites to external contractors who shouldn't use org SSO? We should support a per-invite override (visible only to org owners) with extra confirmation and a logged audit reason. Shows up in audit log as "SSO bypass: reason".
liam: That ties into audit log navigation: when an admin clicks an audit entry for an invite, we should surface a CTA "Open in Invite drawer (pre-filled)". That drawer should be read-only if the invite already sent. Add a note: "This invite used SSO bypass" if applicable.
alexa: Implementation note: for the pre-filled drawer prefer query params like ?invite_audit=1&email=foo@bar.com&bypass=true but mark as read-only server-side for stability.
ben: Design microcopy: confirmation modal for SSO bypass: title: "Bypass SSO for this invite?" body: "This will allow the invited user to sign in without your org SSO. This action will be recorded in the audit log." primary: "Bypass and send" secondary: "Cancel". Keep it short.
priya: For mobile, the pill/menu should collapse into a single line: "SSO: Required" with a chevron that expands full options. Short copy there is crucial.
liam: Another accessibility bit: audit log CTA linking back to Roles or Invite should use rel=noopener and target=_blank to avoid losing context, but also include an aria-describedby to explain it opens a new tab.
alexa: Edge case UX: if SSO settings change after an invite is queued (rare concurrency), the invite drawer should show a subtle banner: "SSO settings changed since this invite was composed. Review before sending."
ben: For the roles matrix, when highlighting rows from audit navigation, we should also show a small inline legend that explains why the row is highlighted (changed role, new invite, bypass). Tooltip with timestamp and actor.
priya: Copy suggestion for legend: "Highlighted from audit: role changed by Priya on Mar 2" (we'll localize later).
liam: Dev question: how often do admins use the per-invite override? If low we hide the option behind an experiment flag to reduce UI surface. I'll check metrics.
alexa: Action items: 1) update invite drawer mock with SSO pill + kebab + domain hint (ben) 2) copy variants for toggle, bypass modal, and audit legend (priya) 3) dev metric check for bypass usage and query param handling (liam) 4) accessibility checklist + aria notes (ben & access-bot).
priya: I'll also add a small microcopy variant for mobile.
ben: I'll prototype the kebab interactions and keyboard flows.
liam: Will post bypass usage by EOD Thursday.
alexa: Thanks team. We'll review mocks in tomorrow's review. :raised_hands:
